bull.b: Costco’s membership model provides recurring revenue that is less dependent on merchandise markup, while high renewal rates indicate durable customer loyalty. Growth in executive and total memberships also supports repeat visits, larger baskets, and a stronger economic foundation for the warehouse model.

Broad-based sales growth and market-share gains suggest Costco is taking a larger share of consumer spending rather than relying on a single category. Expansion across food, electronics, health and beauty, and other departments improves resilience and supports continued scale benefits.

Rising operating and free cash flow gives Costco resources to fund warehouse expansion, digital infrastructure, and shareholder returns internally. At the same time, materially lower leverage reduces balance-sheet risk and preserves flexibility to invest through changing retail conditions.

bear.b: Costco’s low-markup model leaves profitability sensitive to merchandise mix, inflation, and cost changes. Recent gross-margin pressure, including the effect of faster growth in gas, e-commerce, and pharmacy, could constrain earnings conversion even if sales remain strong.

Membership fees are a key profit driver, so slower member growth can reduce the pace of recurring revenue and profit expansion. Although renewal rates remain high, normalization in new sign-ups may make future gains more dependent on warehouse openings, retention, and higher spending.

Pricing changes in pharmacy can pressure revenue quality and margins in a growing ancillary business. Costco has offset the initial impact with script growth and value programs, but continued reimbursement and GLP-1 pricing changes may remain a structural drag on pharmacy profitability.
